newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo NBY leaves discount rate unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Yugo NBY leaves discount rate unchanged.

text.p: The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) left its key discount rate for July unchanged at 2.5 percent per month, a central bank official told Reuters on Tuesday.
This is the fifth consecutive month that the discount rate stayed unchanged at an annual 33.74 percent.
The discount rate, used by the central bank as an instrument for regulating the amount of cash in circulation, was last cut in March after being kept steady at a monthly 4.5 percent since June 1996.

NBY sets its discount rate each month using a basket that includes interest rates on the open money market and its short-term bonds, price rises, expected monetary developments, credit demand and money supply.

A negative 0.1 percent June inflation was insufficient to justify a fresh cut in the discount rate because M1 money supply figures indicate an expansion in the key monetary aggregate over the past two months, an NBY source said.
M1 money supply rose to 5.8 billion dinars ($1.01 billion) in May from 5.562 billion in April. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
